title: Microsoft stock price rally after earnings provides blueprint for AI trade
excerpt: The company struck the perfect chord of blockbuster cloud-computing results and restrained capex spending.
content_html:
Microsoft just laid the market blueprint for other AI giants — and its stock jumped the most in 18 years

By William Edwards

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

It's hard to imagine Microsoft turning in a better earnings report.

Not only did the tech giant post strong growth in its AI-powered Azure cloud-computing business, it also refrained from raising its capex-spending forecast.

Investors went nuts over the report, pushing Microsoft shares up 16%, their biggest single-day jump since 2008.

Microsoft's market success did well to lay out a blueprint for hyperscalers hoping to get investors excited again: Show that you're starting to monetize AI, and don't revise your spending projections upward. If you do that, investors will reward you.

It also reinvigorated a market that sold off sharp on Wednesday following Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's post-FOMC address. Here's a rundown of the gains across the market:

  • S&P 500: 7,438.72, up 1.7%
  • Dow Jones Industrial Average: 52,209.57, up 1.2%
  • Nasdaq 100: 28,106.35, up 3.4%

The chipmaking sector — which has been the foremost lightning rod for AI-spending jitters — got a particularly big boost. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index soared 8%, while Micron, Intel, and AMD each spiked double digits.

Microsoft's market-moving earnings report contrasted sharply with that of its fellow hyperscaler Meta.

Meta issued a disappointing sales forecast while simultaneously raising capex projections. Its stock fell 8%.

Meta-specific concerns aside, Microsoft may have just shown the market that there's a fine line hyperscalers can walk in their spending strategy, one that allows them to both remain competitive and project at least some image of capital discipline.

Jeff Fratarcangeli, the managing principal of Fratarcangeli Wealth Management, told Business Insider earlier this week that it's a line he hopes to see more companies walk in the future. While he doesn't think it's prudent for companies to pull back on capex, he said firms can acknowledge investors' concerns.

"I kind of want to see them play both sides of that," Fratarcangeli said.

"They can say things in a fashion that doesn't necessarily irritate the investors," he continued, "yet still say they're going to be competitive."

很难想象微软会提交一份更好的收益报告。

这家科技巨头不仅在人工智能驱动的 Azure 云计算业务上实现了强劲增长，而且还没有提高资本支出预测。

投资者对该报告感到疯狂，推动微软股价上涨 16%，这是自 2008 年以来的最大单日涨幅。

微软的市场成功很好地为超大规模企业制定了蓝图，希望让投资者再次兴奋起来：表明您正在开始将人工智能货币化，并且不要向上修改您的支出预测。 如果你这样做，投资者就会奖励你。

这也重振了周三在美联储主席凯文·沃什发表联邦公开市场委员会会议后讲话后大幅抛售的市场。 以下是整个市场收益的概要：

  • S&P 500: 7,438.72, up 1.7%
  • 道琼斯工业平均指数：52,209.57，上涨1.2%
  • 纳斯达克100指数：28,106.35，上涨3.4%

芯片制造行业——一直是人工智能支出紧张的最重要的避雷针——得到了特别大的提振。 费城半导体指数飙升 8%，美光、英特尔和 AMD 均上涨两位数。

微软影响市场的盈利报告与其同行超大规模公司 Meta 的盈利报告形成鲜明对比。

Meta 发布了令人失望的销售预测，同时提高了资本支出预测。 其股价下跌 8%。

抛开元特定的担忧不谈，微软可能刚刚向市场表明，超大规模企业可以在他们的支出策略中遵循一条细线，这一策略使他们既能保持竞争力，又能至少展现出一定的资本纪律形象。

Fratarcangeli 财富管理公司的管理负责人 Jeff Fratarcangeli 本周早些时候告诉《商业内幕》，他希望未来看到更多的公司走这条路线。 虽然他认为公司削减资本支出并不明智，但他表示公司可以承认投资者的担忧。

“我有点想看到他们在这两个方面都发挥作用，”弗拉塔坎杰利说。

“他们可以用一种不一定会激怒投资者的方式说一些话，”他继续说道，“但仍然说他们将具有竞争力。”
